newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-General Cable rated buy at 2 firms.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-General Cable rated buy at 2 firms.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co and Dillon Read & Co Inc both started coverage of General Cable Corp with a buy rating on Tuesday, both firms said.
-- Merrill named the stock a Focus One and rated the stock as an intermediate, long-term buy.
-- Dillon Read analyst Thomas O'Halloran said the company has a broad product line, leading market share, improving margins, and a strong management team.
-- O'Halloran said the stock is undervalued, trading at 9.7 times his 1998 earnings estimate of $2.35 a share. He set a 12- to 18-month price target of $40 a share.
-- The stock had not yet opened for trading on the New York Stock Exchange due to an order imbalance. It closed at 22-3/4. It was bid at 24-1/2 and asked at 25-1/2, according to the NYSE.
-- Dillon Read was the lead underwriter of the company's mid-May IPO. Shares sold for $21 each.
-- General Cable, which makes copper wire and cable products, was previously a subsidiary of Wassall Plc. Wassall currently owns roughly 20 percent.

-- Dillon Read says the lynchpin for company's track record of 15-percent-plus earnings growth is its broad product line, allowing it to be a single-source supplier to many customers. It offers 11,000 products to 8,500 customers, "one of the most diverse product lines in the industry," O'Halloran said in the report.
